title: Up-regulation of caveolin 1 mediated by chitosan activates Wnt/ beta-catenin pathway in chronic refractory wound diabetic rat model.
authors: Gao, Jie; Zhang, Jiayuan; Xia, Lianheng; Liang, Xuewei; Ding, Wukun; Song, Meiyu; Li, Linggen; Jia, Zhen
one_liner_zh: 该文研究壳聚糖上调CAV1与beta-catenin互作激活Wnt通路促进糖尿病伤口愈合，虽含蛋白互作和蛋白对接，但对象为蛋白-蛋白而非蛋白-DNA，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) can be implicated in the perturbations of vascular integrity and the dysfunction of angiogenesis. Chitosan has the advantage of promoting the vascular endothelial cell proliferation. However, the molecular mechanism of action in the promotion of wound healing by chitosan derivatives is still debated. In the current study, DM with chronic wound (CW) model rats were prepared and treated with chitosan. Vascular endothelial cells isolated from granulation tissues were conducted by RNA sequencing. Two thousand three hundred and sixteen genes were up-regulated, while 1,864 genes were down-regulated after chitosan treatment compared to CW group. Here, we observed that caveolin 1 (CAV1) was highly expressed induced by chitosan. Furthermore, we observed that CAV1 knockdown could compromise the activation of Wnt pathway by reduction of beta-catenin in rat aortic endothelial cells (RAOECs) and brain endothelium four cells (RBE4s). Moreover, we determined a direct interaction between CAV1 and beta-catenin by IP assay. The C-terminus of CAV1 and beta-catenin (24 to 586 amino acids) contributed to the interaction of these two proteins. Finally, the protein docking analysis indicated that the fragments of beta-catenin (253-261 'FYAITTLHN' and 292-303 'KFLAITTDCLQI') might have affected the structure by CAV1 and facilitated the resistance to degradation. Taken together, our study demonstrates that chitosan can up-regulate CAV1 expression, and CAV1 can interact with beta-catenin for promotion of canonical Wnt signaling pathway activity. Our results deepens the molecular mechanism of the Wnt pathway in vascular endothelial cells and is beneficial to developing new targets to assist in enhancing the pharmacological effect of chitosan on wound healing and angiogenesis against DM.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病（DM）可涉及血管完整性的扰动和血管生成功能障碍。壳聚糖具有促进血管内皮细胞增殖的优势。然而，壳聚糖衍生物促进伤口愈合的分子作用机制仍存在争议。在本研究中，制备了糖尿病伴慢性伤口（CW）模型大鼠并给予壳聚糖处理。从肉芽组织中分离的血管内皮细胞进行了RNA测序。与CW组相比，壳聚糖处理后共有2,316个基因上调，1,864个基因下调。在此，我们观察到壳聚糖诱导的caveolin 1（CAV1）高表达。此外，我们观察到在大鼠主动脉内皮细胞（RAOECs）和脑内皮四细胞（RBE4s）中，CAV1敲低可通过减少β-catenin来损害Wnt通路的激活。而且，我们通过免疫沉淀（IP）实验确定了CAV1与β-catenin之间的直接相互作用。CAV1的C末端和β-catenin（第24至586个氨基酸）促成了这两种蛋白质的相互作用。最后，蛋白质对接分析表明，β-catenin的片段（253-261 'FYAITTLHN' 和 292-303 'KFLAITTDCLQI'）可能通过CAV1影响结构，并促进对降解的抵抗。综上所述，我们的研究表明，壳聚糖可上调CAV1表达，且CAV1可与β-catenin相互作用以促进经典Wnt信号通路活性。我们的结果深化了Wnt通路在血管内皮细胞中的分子机制，并有助于开发新靶点，以增强壳聚糖在对抗糖尿病中促进伤口愈合和血管生成的药理作用。
